We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}={x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}{log}_{2}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{2}⁡(x))(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})-\int (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}{log}_{2}⁡(x)}{3}-\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{9\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$
